result:
**Verdict: FAIL** on DG6 round 5, candidate `sha256:832e5c82…14988` (2740 files, source `d7b21bad3`). Both of my open findings are now fixed and verified. I raised one new Medium finding, which has to be repaired before the gate (D-192).

Before starting I confirmed the candidate. HEAD (`518b0c9f0`) is the freeze commit on top of the source commit and adds only freeze metadata. The candidate ID recomputes to the frozen value in the repository and in my clone, with no file missing or mismatched. All validators pass: `--register DG6` and `--historical` for DG5 down to DG1.

**Open findings, both CLOSED_VERIFIED**
- **F-DG6-280 (High, mandatory): fixed.**
  - My round-4 reproduction now passes. The Transformation Lead (TL), who gets 404 on the sensitive benefit and its corrective case, is refused when naming the case (422, the same answer as for an unknown id). No executive ask is created.
  - A new probe through the real worker consumers confirms the rest:
    - a case opened after the benefit is marked sensitive is titled by its own code;
    - an admitted user's escalation creates the ask titled "CA-01";
    - the TL, Auditor and Sponsor never see the benefit title in the ask list, detail, inbox or search (the search index was really built);
    - the Transformation Office still sees the title.
  - The same holds in the UI, in English and Arabic.
  - Putting back the round-4 code makes 8 of 10 tests fail.
- **F-DG6-281 (Low): fixed.** The connector edit screen now shows "A transformation you cannot view · <id>" (and the Arabic equivalent) with a hint, and saving keeps the stored target. Putting back the round-4 screen makes 2 of 29 unit tests fail.

**New findings**
- **F-DG6-340 (Medium, not mandatory; owner backend-workflow-engineer).** Report tables now hide a restricted benefit's row, but its value stays in the total with no "Includes restricted records" label. That breaks the labelling rule the user decided (D-195 Q3, ADR-0051 §2).
  - In my test, the Transformation Lead's benefits register shows one row at 0.0000 and a validated total of 250000, which is exactly the hidden benefit's value, with nothing to explain it.
  - The benefit-totals screen does show the label for the same user.
  - The snapshot page shows the totals with no label, in English and Arabic.
  - The BE-Z5 handback and the register disclose this gap, but D-214 left it undecided.
- **F-DG6-341 (Low, documentation only; owner solution-architect).** ADR-0053 still describes a strict version check for acknowledging and resolving exceptions. The shipped BE-Z6 rule, which tolerates intervening system re-raises, is not recorded there, although the BE-Z6 handback asked for it.

**Open questions you asked me to judge**
- **BE-Z6 is sound.** A conflict between two humans still returns 409, and no system update is lost. Resolving an exception that recurred after the page loaded is acceptable: the next failure opens a new exception.
- **The other BE-Z5 residuals are acceptable:**
  - the 71 operations the sweep cannot fill;
  - the search index, which I exercised myself;
  - stored rows created before the fix;
  - benefit ids in the frozen G6 snapshot;
  - the counts kept as truthful verdicts.
- **The escalation is still useful to its users.** The TL sees "DEC-01 · CA-01" with its origin; the Transformation Office follows it to the case.
- **Decisions accepted:** D-194 to D-196, D-199 item 2, D-202 and D-203 to D-205.

**Full runs on the candidate**

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| QA integration | 45/45 files, 437 tests passed |
| Implementer P6 integration | 49/49 files, 584 tests passed |
| Root P6 end-to-end (production stack) | 38/38 passed |
| A20 UX, accessibility and term scan | 226 passed; the 18 skips are the declared unscanned axe routes |
| Demo-stack end-to-end | 12/12 passed |
| Unit, Node 24.21.0 | 2899 + 2054 tests passed, exit 0 |
| Unit, Node 22.22.0 (the assignment says 22.22.2) | same counts, exit 0 |

The unit runs needed reruns under heavy machine load, and every failed run is disclosed in the record:
- the first Node 24 run had five timing failures, plus one test that failed only because my sparse clone had left out an evidence folder;
- the first Node 22 run was stopped by my own time limit;
- three later runs passed every test but exited 1 on a vitest internal timeout.

My own probe runs that failed are also disclosed: a wrong table name in my probe, a database permission error in my test setup, and a missing business calendar on the test stack. None of these is a product defect. The environmental residuals (Keycloak, live registry and CI, real external systems, production capacity) are recorded as PASS on their offline surfaces, as the assignment instructs.

All three files validate against the schemas, and every evidence path exists. The disposable clone and scratch files have been removed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-5/`:
- `domain-reviewer.json`
- `domain-reviewer.verifications.json`
- `domain-reviewer.findings.json`

Evidence, including the English and Arabic screenshots, is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/domain/round-5/`.
